Into this love the divine instructors are led by the Savior becoming a pattern for them, as the God-wise Evangelist John calls out to those who worship God according to Christ: 'That He,' clearly that Christ, 'set His soul as a ransom for us, and we owe to lay down our souls for one another' (1 John 3:16).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The Lord threatens to hand the land over to tyrants because the shepherds despised the flock, and he repeats the threat so that those threatened may stop sinning.
comments.comment: Since those entrusted with the care of the logical sheep despised them, neither sympathizing with nor caring for their salvation, but selling them to strangers through shameful gain, the Lord Almighty threatens no longer to spare the land, that is, those dwelling upon it, handing over the weaker ones to the tyrants through whom they suppose to have strength and brutality, so that all those upon the land may be cut down, handing over every man into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king, no longer by lawful means but by tyrannical rule. … God repeats these things in the manner of a threat, so that those toward whom the threat is directed may cease from sinning through the fear of what is expected.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why God threatens not to spare and what the threat is for.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: God's refusal to spare those on the earth is a warning given so that they may leave their sin, and handing them over to neighbors and tyrants teaches them through harm.
comments.comment: Having these things thus, if God says: 'I will no longer spare those dwelling on the earth,' He admonishes by the fear of threat, so that they might not fall by being executed, but might come out of the sin that holds fast, no longer being subject to execution. He makes manifest the manner of not sparing anymore, saying 'to deliver men into the hands of their neighbors and into the hands' of the 'evil king whom they chose, so that the earth might be cut off' (Zechariah 11:6), as they oppose one another as 'men who are dying.' These are those walking according to the flesh in strife and jealousy. Men who are such are delivered into the hands of those whom they had as neighbors, namely demons, through greed and material disposition. For then they are most able to be admonished, having been delivered to those whom they thought were friends and neighbors, having been tested by their coarseness and ferocity; and they will flee also from the one who rules tyrannically, having experienced his hardness. For even the people of the Hebrews desired in such a way to be set free from the insolence of the Egyptians, having known their turbulence and their lawless dominion. … When the earth is cut off, that is, when those upon it are revolting, God shepherds the sheep of the slaughter into Canaan, the prepared punishment. It was also said previously that the sheep of the slaughter are those ready to suffer and those already slaughtered, when we received that which was being reported by the afflicted to the Benefactor of all: 'You gave us as sheep for eating' (Psalm 44:11), and again: 'We were counted as sheep for slaughter' (Psalm 44:22). Understand whether the shepherding of the sheep of the slaughter into Canaan denotes something praiseworthy, being interpreted as the prepared place, perhaps of those being led in through being managed by harm. … Working out an unchangeable salvation through pains brought on pedagogically, about which the law-giving apostle Paul writes, marking these things: 'The godly sorrow works out unchangeable repentance unto salvation, bringing about the death of the sorrow of the world' (2 Cor 7:10). Therefore, this worldly sorrow must be rejected, but the godly one must be unchangeably opposed, bringing about salvation according to God.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The two rods are scepters of kingship, for God took both the Jews and the Gentiles to make one kingship under one king and one flock under one shepherd.
comments.comment: From the person of the Savior, the prophet Zechariah 11:7 announces the things concerning the two rods which he had taken for himself. … Nothing else is signified in the passages concerning the rods except a scepter of rule, rather a symbol of kingship. … Since therefore the whole human race is divided into the people from the circumcision and into the Church called from the Gentiles, the God of the Jews and the Gentiles, being both Savior and King of them, took for himself the two scepters, so that from both he might work out one kingship. … And the prophecy will be understood from the evangelical utterance; for just as one kingship was shown under one king from those having believed among the Gentiles and the Jews, so also one flock is shown under one shepherd, the true one, who has set his soul down for the sheep. Thus the evangelical voice is announced by the Savior: 'And I have other sheep which are not of this fold; them also I must bring together, and they will hear my voice, so that there will become one flock and one shepherd' (John 10:16), saying that the other sheep are to be those from the Gentiles believing in the Gospel, not from the Jewish fold. … It is the same thing, the two flocks becoming under one shepherd, as it is the two scepters coming under the same king.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the two rods are and how they point to one flock and one shepherd.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The two rods are the two peoples, from the circumcision and from the Gentiles, joined into one scepter of kingship in Christ, who made both one.
comments.comment: When the harmony of the prophetic enigma has appeared regarding the division of the one rule into two kingdoms and the restoration of these into one rule according to the prophecy of Hosea, it follows, having been read through the history, to understand the things concerning the two rods which the Son of Man took for himself. … For it must be understood through them the callings of the two peoples, both from the nations and from the circumcision, joined into one scepter of kingship, according to the meaning of the apostolic writing, which says: 'He is our peace, who makes both the two one and having broken down the middle wall of the partition, so that he might create the two in himself as one new man' (Ephesians 2:14), the Greek and the Jew. For when one was Judaizing and the other was Hellenizing, two rods and two men existed, divided by the difference of religion, as if they were not under one king. … Of the two having become one rod of rule, one was raised by the Father, the one according to the flesh who was raised by God from David, who having become an eternal shepherd and king according to humanity, having been shown to be the leader of a peaceful and eternal covenant, will rule steadfastly and peacefully for ever unto the ages, his kingdom never ceasing. … And this good thing will exist perfectly when 'the fullness of the Gentiles having entered' (Rom 11:25), into the highest blessedness, 'all Israel shall be saved' (Rom 11:26).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The soul of God is weighed down by the three shepherds because they savaged the flock, and when the true shepherd says he will not shepherd them, they are lost to the harmful ones.
comments.comment: This so-called soul of God is weighed down by the three shepherds being removed in a single month, being indignant at the one who removed them from the Savior. And their removal happens because, like the manner of lions, their souls were being torn by savagery against the true shepherd. … Since the coarseness of the shepherds is described, the good chief-shepherd, regarding the sheep lost by the wicked shepherds, says in the manner of the threat 'I will not shepherd you,' especially since they were still being lost by the harmful ones; for they had not yet been removed; for 'I will remove the three shepherds' shows that they were at the height of being placed over the flocks led astray by them.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: When the shepherd leaves the flock because of the idleness of the shepherds, the sheep fall into savagery and devour one another, whereas under the good shepherd each is cared for and lacks nothing.
comments.comment: Under the good shepherd overseeing the flock, each of the sheep is cared for in the necessary way. … just as each of those completing the divine flock cries out concerning the shepherd: “The Lord shepherds me, and I shall lack nothing. In a place of green pasture, there He has made me abide; by the waters of rest He has nourished me, He has restored my soul. He has led me upon the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name.” … Thus, when the spiritual nourishment is neglected due to their own idleness, left behind by the one saying, “I will not shepherd you,” the opposite happens to the flocks, such that the dying indeed die, having been distanced from the one saying, the shepherd, concerning his own sheep: “I came that they might have life and have it abundantly, having laid down my life for the sheep.” … By this savagery, the Church of the Galatians having fallen, it is fittingly written against her by the apostle Paul: “But if you bite and devour one another, see that you are not consumed by one another.”
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The staff cast away is the royal scepter, the calling of the Church from the nations, who are the Canaanites prepared as the inheritance of the Son of God.
comments.comment:
Because the people of circumcision were abandoned by the shepherd due to their unfaithfulness toward him, the lying ones encountered the consequences, as if the dying were dying and the vanishing were vanishing, and the remnants were turned to eat the flesh of their neighbor. … A calling occurs of the Church from the nations having believed in Christ, which he also named a praiseworthy staff, that is, a kingdom, saying: "And I will take the good staff." But this surpassed what the Father said to the Son: "Ask from me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance."

Because the royal scepter was cast away by the one having taken all the nations as inheritance, the covenant toward all the peoples was scattered, concerning which it is said in Deuteronomy in a great song in this manner: "When the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the angels of God." This covenant having been scattered by Christ, the angels no longer presiding over the nations, an inheritance and a portion has become all the nations of the one who cast away the good staff upon the dissolution of the covenant toward all the peoples. … Having endured these divine exploits, the Canaanites shall know, being sheep being guarded, "that it is the word of the Lord" regarding the lying ones... … Being a signifier of great and exceeding mysteries, which it is necessary to understand, it is both a rod and a covenant toward all the peoples. … The Canaanites were being called out from the nations, prepared to become the inheritance of the Son of God …
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The prophetic words abruptly change the persons who speak, and here the Savior speaks to the Jews, asking for his wages.
comments.comment: The prophetic words, being uttered enigmatically, abruptly change the persons of those speaking and of whom they speak … See how many changes of persons are brought about in these few symbols, not being dispersed according to the letter but in the understanding. … Just as it is regarding the received testimony, so it is in the voice of Zechariah having been set forth. For the Savior having said—for He himself is the one announcing the things set before regarding the rejection of those of the circumcision—and having announced furthermore regarding the calling of the nations who formerly were idolaters, He says from another beginning: 'I was answered and I said to them,' that is, to the Jews: 'If it is good and just in your sight, give, that is to say, having determined, my wages; but if not, refuse, declining...'
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Silver in Scripture often signifies the divine word, though some silver is reproached as a deceitful word, so the thirty pieces of silver are a wage measured in words.
comments.comment: It is appropriate to receive both a wage and silver. Often, the divine teachings and the word are signified by this name: 'The words of the Lord are pure words, like silver refined in a furnace, tested, cleansed in the earth seven times' (Ps 12:6). And again, it is said proverbially: 'The tongue of the righteous is like refined silver' (Prov 10:20). For the word is signified by the name of the tongue. … And since not all silver mentioned allegorically is praised, but some is also reproached, thus God says to the false teachers of Israel: 'Your silver is worthless' (Isaiah 1:22); He does not mean a physical coin, but a deceitful word. … This understanding is the proverbial ordinance brought forth thus: 'Silver given with deceit should be regarded as shards.' For the deceptive and contentious word brought forth with deceit by sophists—even if it seems to be about great things, the so-called 'exaltations, puffed up according to the knowledge of God'—is to be announced as being to be regarded as shards; such are those who are described as 'those who set their minds on earthly things' (Philippians 3:19), whom Isaiah said are 'those shouting from the earth' (Isaiah 8:19).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The Father tells the Savior to cast the thirty pieces of silver into the treasury and test it, so that it will be shown whether he gives worthily the wage for which he accepted toil on their behalf.
comments.comment: Since there is indeed a difference between logical silvers, having established the wage of those of the circumcision against those who toil over them as thirty pieces of silver, the Father says to the one having received the thirty pieces of silver: 'Cast them into the treasury and test if it is worthy' (Zechariah 11:13), the silver given, 'in the manner in which I was tested' on their behalf. For thus it will be revealed whether I am providing worthily the wage for which I accepted toil on their behalf, 'laying down my life and giving it as a ransom for many' (Mk 10:45). … Having said these things of the Father, I say this: Cast the thirty pieces of silver into the treasury, the one 'having become obedient unto death' (Phil 2:8) without hesitation, following what was commanded; they took, He says, the silver and threw it into the house of the Lord into the treasury (Zechariah 11:13).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Counterfeit silver is the deceitful word, exposed in God's house both in those who tested the Savior and in Christians who twist Scripture, while genuine silver bears the Savior's image.
comments.comment:
The reward of circumcision is deceitful, just as those searching the scriptures which testify concerning the Savior as he spoke them have considered it to be a counterfeit coin. … For often in the Gospels the wicked word of those being accused is exposed, as in: 'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; and in vain they worship me, teaching commandments of men as doctrines' (Matt 15:8), nullifying the commandment of God through their harmful tradition. Likewise, those proposing an unproven word concerning whether it is necessary to give tribute to Caesar or not are exposed, as they themselves were accused of being deceitful and speaking with much cunning from that very moment; for when being asked, the Savior said: 'Show me the coin' (Matt 22:19), meaning 'whose image and inscription it has.' And those saying: 'Caesar's,' were strongly rebated upon hearing: 'Therefore render to Caesar the things of Caesar, and to God the things of God' (Matt 22:21).

And not only do the Jews approaching the Savior in a testing manner possess an unproven word, but also the heretics in Christianity who pseudo-doctrinalize, 'walking in cunning and deceiving the word of the Lord,' diverting and distorting the will of the God-breathed oracles; whom one must also reject, considering their deceitful word to be as counterfeit silver. Is the word of those setting two unbegotten principles, good and evil—and these are Manichaeans—not unproven? And is it not unproven of those saying the Son is a creature and dividing the Holy Spirit from Father and Son? And is it not unproven of the impious ones regarding the incarnation of the Savior, those thinking the Savior appeared and was not true? Not only is the counterfeit silver made manifest from the crucible of the house of God, but also the genuine silver bearing the image and character of the All-King Savior, 'having been purified sevenfold,' which must be held and in which one must prosper by possession. … They are grasping that those whom Judas received, thirty pieces of silver from the Jews in order that he might betray the Lord (Matt 26:15), are signified also from the spoken word, and this is the greatest indictment of the Jews who gave and of Judas who received the thirty pieces of silver for betrayal.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Blasphemies against the crucified Savior are to be cast into the house of the writings, to convict those who bring them.
comments.comment: It is necessary to cast the blasphemies, which the Jews bring against the Savior crucified for the sake of the whole creation, into the house of the God-breathed writings and into the vessel contained therein, so that they may be convicted of being unheeding, rather than opposing the prophecies concerning Christ and his cross.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The cast-away staff is the one nation of the Hebrews, whose one kingdom was divided in two and is restored to one under a single king by the grace of the Savior.
comments.comment: Our Savior and Lord has taken two rods, the beauty of which he first summoned, having previously cast away that called beauty, revealing the mysteries already made clear; now, having cast away the one called the staff, he scattered the covenant between Israel and Judah. … What is the staff called the staff? From the great song it is again to be learned. And the things of the song are held thus, as they were previously set forth: 'When the Most High divided the nations, as he scattered the sons of Adam, he set boundaries of nations according to the number of the angels of God, and there became a divided people of the Lord, his Jacob, a staff of inheritance, his Israel.' These things are said concerning the whole nation of the Hebrews being one rod and one portion. And for a long time the whole nation remained unsuitably acting as one rod, according to that which is proclaimed in the Psalms to the King and Forethinker of all: 'Remember your assembly, which I will gather from the beginning; I will redeem the rod of your inheritance.' … This one kingdom was divided into two leaderships, as Judah is called, and Ephraim, with those remaining in Jerusalem having the succession under the house of David from the tribe of Judah, and those having descended into Samaria having Jeroboam as leader, having sinned against Israel, being from the tribe of Ephraim. … And for a long time the wickedness of the division remained, with the king of Judah and the tyrant of Samaria apostatizing and contending against one another, until God may have mercy, and again show the twelve tribes as one kingdom … Concerning this restoration, it is brought forth in Hosea the prophet, the All-King saying: 'The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah shall be gathered, and they shall set for themselves one beginning and shall ascend from the land, because great is the day of Jezreel' (Hosea 1:11). … One must attend to the prophecy declaring that those being restored into one kingdom ascend from the land, making it clear that they exist down in the land, having been scattered by their own division away from the single hegemony. After the covenant of the schism having worked in the midst of Judah and Israel for a time, a scattering and a resolution of it occurs by the grace of the Savior, so that from the departure of the difference of the schisms, the so-called splintered rod might become one under a single king as before, he having the succession from Judah, so that there might be one flock and one shepherd existing under the lawful king of the whole nation.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the second staff is and why its breaking scatters the covenant.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The prophet took the vessels of an inexperienced shepherd, which may foretell a destructive shepherd such as the Antichrist, who eats the flesh of the sheep dear to him.
comments.comment: Since, therefore, regarding an inexperienced shepherd lacking the art of shepherding, the holy one receiving God had to understand the listeners, he perceived the spoken vessels sensually, so that he might speak about them and what they signify when asked by those seeing that he had taken up shepherd's vessels not as an experienced man but as an inexperienced one. Much is thus managed in the prophets, especially in Ezekiel. It is not unlikely that things concerning the Antichrist, regarding such a destructive shepherd, are pre-announced, as is found in many writings. … He said, 'the elect sheep, whose flesh he eats,' not absolutely and truly the elect, but those chosen as dear and familiar to the one eating their flesh.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The sword on the arm and eye of the worthless shepherd is the punishing word of God, which dries up his work and blinds the eye he thought was right.
comments.comment: 'O you who shepherd the vain and who have abandoned the sheep: a sword upon his arm and upon his right eye; his arm being dried shall be dried, and his right eye being blinded shall be blinded' (Zech 11:17). Rather than merely blaming, the divine word threatens the false shepherds who have turned away and abandoned the sheep, hunting the vain, making shameful gain manifest, and the destruction of the flesh which they were entrusted to nourish, as concerning each of them or as if all were done through the same wickedness: 'A sword upon the arm,' that is, his work. Often it has been demonstrated that the arm signifies, according to allegory, a work. … What then is the sword upon the arm and eye of the wicked shepherd? Either the punitive word of which God says in Isaiah to those who follow the law: 'If you are willing and would obey, you shall eat the good of the land; but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured by the sword' (Isa 1:19-20). … The aforementioned punitive sword, having come upon the arm and the eye, that is, upon the practical power and the contemplative power, like a punishing shepherd dries the arm, removing all moisture and soft suppleness so that it may be deadened. And it will blind the eye and blind it, the one which seems to the possessor to be right, but not being such in truth, but being crooked and left and perhaps something even more inferior. … And these words were also struck by the Antichrist, promising to have a strong and living arm through the signs and wonders which he performs, being false, and a right eye, partaking of the glance of the haughty king of the Assyrians …
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The spirit of man that God shapes within him is the hidden man of the heart, shaped not as a body is but by virtue, as in the prayer 'Create in me a clean heart.'
comments.comment:
The spirit of a man being shaped within him is that about which the Apostle writes: 'Who knows the things of man, except the spirit of the man that is in him' (1 Cor 2:11), being something different from the rational soul, known as the 'hidden man of the heart'.'

The shaping of it is not like that of the body, but is that which the holy hymn-writer prays should exist in his heart, saying: 'Create in me a clean heart, O God' (Ps 51:10). And a clean heart is being shaped according to virtue and being stamped by another holiness, so that it may act and think strongly and harmoniously.

This opinion, which belonged to Judith, who struck down the tyrant Holofernes, the wisest elders, praising her, said to her: 'Good is the formation of your heart' (Judith 9:11).
comments.selected_reason: Explains what it means that God shapes the spirit of man within him.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The soul is not shaped by hands from matter but inspired by divine power.
comments.comment: Just as another [the prophet] has said, "He who formed the spirit of man within him" (Zechariah 12:1). … For the work is not divided. Even if the making of the soul is more beautiful than that of the body, it is not as if made by hands according to the shaping of matter, but inspired according to its subsistence from divine power.
comments.author: Apollinaris of Laodicea

comments.capsule: When Scripture says God forms a human's spirit within him, no one thinks the spirit is another person beside the human, so we must look to the natures of things rather than over-scrutinize the forms of words.
comments.comment: And over one person a double-faced form of speech is often brought in for us, and in no way does it wrong the truth. For example, if inspired Scripture should say about God: “He who forms a human’s spirit within him,” (Zechariah 12:1) yet how is it not clear to all that the spirit formed within him would not be understood as another beside the human? And the blessed David says somewhere: “At night I conversed with my heart, and I stirred my spirit.” (Psalm 77:6) Then who was the one conversing with his own heart and probing his own spirit? Therefore one must not over-scrutinize the forms of the words, but rather look to the natures of the things themselves, and being well guided from them go to the truth itself.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On the True Faith, to the Empresses Pulcheria and Eudocia

comments.capsule: The Creator who shaped the spirit of man threatens to lay waste Jerusalem because of those who struck the Savior, so that it has no seat or security left, abandoned by the one who founded and guards it.
comments.comment: He who stretched out the heavens, laid the foundation of the earth, and shaped the spirit of man within him, threatens to lay waste and overthrow the city and land of the Jews because of the audacity of the atheists who struck at the Savior who had arrived—for indeed, with cross and blows He surrounded the one who gave His soul as a ransom, the one who bore the sin of the world—even though He had come for the salvation of all. … And what is it that is being pre-announced as a harsh thing against those who killed Christ? 'Behold, I set Jerusalem as a shaking threshold, and Judea around all the peoples' … He says, meaning that it no longer has any seat or security, having been abandoned by the one who founded and guards it, fulfilling the manner of the threat pre-announced in Isaiah: 'The daughter of Zion shall be left forsaken' (Isaiah 1:8) … For before the leaving and the handing over, there existed house and inheritance and a beloved soul, concerning which these things are said by the speaker later because of the impiety against him: “Behold, your house is left to you desolate.” (Luke 13:35).
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the threat against Jerusalem is and why it is made.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Because the threatened hardships touched Judah and its city, stone no longer lay upon stone and foreign nations trod the holy ground as if it were a common stone, as Jeremiah and the Savior had foreseen.
comments.comment: And since the threatened hardships touched even the sensible Judah and its metropolis—for it was cast down so that no longer stone lay upon stone—the surrounding peoples of the foreign nations, not being permitted to enter to tread upon the holy ground, tread upon it, as if treading upon a bare and common stone by unwashed feet. … Jeremiah, having foreseen this gloomy thing with a long prophetic gaze, lamenting and wailing for the city falling into such wickedness, spoke mournfully: “How did the city, once filled with people, sit alone? Was the one filled with nations reckoned as a desert?” (Lamentations 1:1). … The Savior, approaching Jerusalem, said that these things would happen to her: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, if you had known also the things toward peace; but now they have been hidden from your eyes; for your enemies, coming, will surround you, making a trench around you,” (Luke 19:42-43) as having been abandoned to be leveled to the ground, all the warring nations having come around you, as to see you desolate: “For when, he says, you see Jerusalem surrounded by encampments, you know that its desolation has approached.”
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The fall of Judea fulfilled what the Savior and Zechariah foretold: the uncircumcised nations mounted Jerusalem and trampled it like an unclean stone, as a field to be plowed.
comments.comment: Concerning this wrath having reached its end so quickly in Judea and those dwelling in it, the writer of their sufferings himself composed a very large collection, describing both them and their places, so as to see unceasingly how fully what the Savior and Zechariah had said prophetically was fulfilled, beginning from: 'I set Jerusalem as a shaking threshold' (Zechariah 12:2). Having set its gates to be shaken, with a surrounding region also shaking it, all the uncircumcised nations, having mounted upon it, trample it contemptuously like an unclean stone, no longer coming as to a temple and a holy ground, unprotected and not with the proper cleansings and purifications. Therefore, mocking, they mock it like a ruin, with all others mounting upon it 'as a field to be plowed' (Micah 3:12).
comments.selected_reason: Explains how the prophecy of Jerusalem as a stone trampled by the nations was fulfilled.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: In the spiritual sense, those who teach falsely build Zion in blood, and the Word of God shakes this false Jerusalem so that all the nations trample and mock it.
comments.comment:
Regarding the spoken word, let that which is toward the intellect also be spoken; all the heretics through whom they think badly and act, 'build Zion in blood and Jerusalem in iniquity' (Micah 3:10). For how is it that they do not build Zion in blood, causing scandal and pouring out the blood of those whom they deceive? Therefore also they build Jerusalem in iniquity. That those being deceived are wronged by the deceivers, the Scripture of the divine Proverbs declares most clearly concerning such things, saying thus: 'They shall be filled with their own impiety; for because they wronged the helpless, they shall be slain, and the scrutiny shall consume the impious' (Proverbs 1:31-32).

The Word of God sets the shaking thresholds for the city being built by hand, so that they might be overthrown by strong reproof, so that it might be trampled by the surrounding peoples, the pseudo-Jerusalem having been shown to be trampled like a defiled stone, so as to mock those who mock the pseudonym, those having known its illegitimacy and uncleanness, who ambassador the truth and the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven. … And since not a few are mocking, but all the nations, in the falling into poverty, it was rightly said that all the nations shall be gathered against it. Jerusalem is trampled like a stone when the sun of righteousness has risen, making a mental day, which has already been much remembered. …
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The false horses are deceitful men whose riders are lying demons, and God tramples them on the day he makes, destroying their wisdom so that their riders fall into folly.
comments.comment: I will trample every horse in frenzy and its rider in folly; and upon the house of Judah I will open my eyes; and I will trample all the horses of the peoples in their blindness. … In the things foretold by the prophet, regarding horses and their riders, a clarity has come in many ways; wherefore most of them are now keeping silence, only remembering for the present need of how this has been seen. Deceitful men, established by lying words, exist as 'false horses for salvation,' having riders and passengers who are deceptive spirits and hypocritical, lying-speaking demons of whom they act as ambassadors for the teaching, putting forward 'the wisdom of this age and of its rulers.' … Those having horses thus, God tramples on the day which He Himself makes, according to what was said in the manner of blessing toward the one being dazzled: 'The Lord shall be to you an eternal light' (Isa 60:19). And God tramples the false horses not because they do not exist at all, but so that they may not perceive concerning those things of which they speak and are being confirmed, with the destruction of their wisdom and the nullification of their understanding; which happening, the rider of each such horse will be in folly.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: God opens his eyes upon the house of Judah, which is the Church of the living God, so that the watchful powers look on those who receive his grace.
comments.comment: This economy having been worked out, God will open His eyes upon the house of Judah, being the 'Church of the living God' (1 Tim 3:15), reigning in it by the Savior having risen from the tribe of Judah, toward whom the theosophists say: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you; your hands are upon the loins of your enemies, and the sons of your father shall worship you' (Genesis 49:8). … Upon this house of Judah, the Benefactor opens His eyes, the overseeing and watchful powers, as each of those receiving the illumination and the grace says in the manner of prayer: 'Look upon me and have mercy on me.' And all the righteous enjoy the gift of the Great King, 'having His eyes upon them and His ears toward their prayer' (Ps 34:15).
comments.selected_reason: Explains what it means that God opens his eyes upon the house of Judah.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The blinding of horses that serve lust is a benefit, since being deprived of sight turns the soul to sobriety, as Elymas was blinded for a time that he might later behold the sun of righteousness.
comments.comment: For the animals that serve lust are struck toward goodness in their blindness, so that they may no longer look sharply toward lust. For this deprivation of the eyes will be received by the soul as an uplift of sobriety, so as to correctly see what remains to be done and what is fitting to work. … Indeed, the sorcerer Elymas, who sees wickedly, was blinded for a time, casting off the vision of deception, so that later, having regained sight, he might behold 'the sun of righteousness.' For it is not useless that the sun, which is to be seen, is seen such that when one has endured blindness, he sees the light.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The commanders of Judah are the apostles and teachers of Christ, who find those of the same faith, citizens of the heavenly Jerusalem who stay unshaken under God.
comments.comment: And the commanders of Judah shall say in their hearts: 'We shall find for ourselves those dwelling in Jerusalem in the Lord of all-ruling God their own' (Zechariah 12:5). Concerning the praiseworthy Judah to whom it is said: 'Judah, your brothers have praised you,' his commanders are those serving under him, the power of the king of all, having been revealed as 'the firstborn and servants of the word,' namely the apostles of Christ. … The one fulfilling this fair city as an excellent and lawful citizen, being steadfast according to holiness and the rest of divine virtue, becomes unshakeable, according to that which is said in Psalm 1 of the steps: 'He who dwells in Jerusalem shall not be moved.' And he dwells in it forever, remaining under the one ruling over it. … And all those presiding over the apostolic Church find those who hold the same faith through right teaching, being citizens of the true and spiritual Jerusalem, as if because of this they dwell in it. Of the leaders who are assigned, the Lord God Almighty is the one holding and ruling them.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The leaders of Judah are set as a firebrand in wood and a torch in a reed, so that the fiery Word consumes the unfruitful and the chaff is burned while the wheat is gathered.
comments.comment: In that day I will set the leaders of Judah as a firebrand among the wood and as a torch of fire in a reed, and they shall consume on the right and on the left all the peoples around, and Jerusalem shall dwell yet for itself (Zechariah 12:6-7). … In the time, the day which he spoke of because of the light, the leaders of Judah find for themselves those dwelling in Jerusalem, being set by God as a firebrand among the wood and as a torch of fire in a reed, so that on the right and on the left all the peoples may be devoured around. As a firebrand among the wood and a torch in a reed, the leaders of the intelligible Judah are set, so that by the fiery and luminous Word they may consume the unfruitful and material volitions. For trees not producing good fruit are being cut down and thrown into the fire; they are wood being handed over to punishment, so that the worst quality of them may be consumed, just as the stalks, being reed and not wheat, are consumed by fire. For it has been said in the Gospel that, when Jesus is cleansing the threshing floor in which he has a winnowing fan in his hand, the wheat is being brought into the storehouse of the promises—these are the righteous men—but the chaff will be burned with unquenchable fire, as the worst volition is consumed when those with private volition are found to be unfruitful (Matthew 3:12).
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the firebrand among wood and the torch in a reed stand for.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The Spirit of grace and mercy is poured out generously by the Father of mercies, as Joel and Paul show.
comments.comment: The generous gift is made manifest by the word, 'I will pour out a spirit of grace and mercy' (Zechariah 12:10), as it can be learned from other sayings; for God says, 'I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh' (Joel 2:28), which signifies a rich giving, just as also, 'The love of God is poured out in our hearts' (Romans 5:5). … From the apostolic voice, it is presented that the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of grace, it being written: 'If anyone violates the law of Moses, he dies upon two or three witnesses without mercies; how much more do you think he will deserve a more severe punishment, he who has trampled the Son of God, and considered the blood of the covenant common, and has insulted the Spirit of grace in whom he was sanctified?' (Hebrews 10:29). … The Spirit of grace and mercy is being supplied by 'the Father of mercies.' It has been said toward this in other commentaries that the God of all is the Father of mercies of the Divine Word and the giver of the Holy Spirit.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the 'spirit of grace and mercy' is and who gives it.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The Jews who struck the Lord, fallen into distress, wail as for a beloved or firstborn son, since Jesus is both the beloved and the only-begotten Son.
comments.comment: Regarding the prophecy: 'And they shall look upon me instead of those whom they have looked upon with contempt, and they shall wail for them as for a beloved, and shall grieve with a grief like that for a firstborn' (Zechariah 12:10). Having fallen into great distress, the Jews who struck the Lord are prevailing with loud wailing and grief, just as if they were wailing for a beloved one who has died and grieving over a firstborn son, 'before the wrath reaches its end upon them,' as if their fatherland were to be dug up and they were to become wandering vagabonds in all the land. … It is probable that the grief is upon the beloved and the pain is upon the firstborn of those who murdered, since the cruel things came upon them, killing Jesus, being a firstborn Son and beloved. … It has been seen many times that 'the beloved' signifies two things: the one worthy of being loved and the Only-begotten Son. But both exist in Jesus Christ, being the Son of love, that is, of God, concerning whom it is written: 'God is love' (1 John 4:8), but also only-begotten, for he is the only-begotten Son from the Father and from the holy Virgin Mary.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The evangelist's 'They shall look upon him whom they pierced' differs in wording from the prophet's text because the evangelist, being a Hebrew, translated the Hebrew himself or took it from another translator such as Aquila.
comments.comment: For he says of the one suffering by them: 'They shall look upon me instead of those from whom they looked down' (Zechariah 12:10). Were they not acting impiously and irreverently when, mocking Jesus being hung as the stake, they said: 'Behold, the one destroying the temple of God and raising it up in three days (Mt 26:61). He saved others, but he is not able to save himself' (Mt 27:42). … These things and other things of the scoundrels mocking, the evangelist writes to be fulfilled by the prophecy having such a character: 'They shall look upon him whom they pierced' (Zech 12:10), which differs in single words from: 'They shall look upon me instead of those from whom they looked down' (Zechariah 12:10). For those having investigated the Hebrew dialect say that the existing text of Zechariah was translated into the evangelical Greek, that is, the evangelist having brought it, for he was a Hebrew; or from another having interpreted and received it, that is, Aquila or Theodotus or someone else having brought the Hebrew word into Greece. … We have been led forward to say these things because some are seeking where it is said among the prophets: 'They shall look upon him whom they pierced' (Zech 12:10), not being found anywhere among those published of the Old Testament.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why John's quotation of the verse reads differently from the prophet's text.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The prophet speaks of one unclean spirit while the apostle speaks of deceiving spirits in the plural, because things taken one by one are commonly called one spirit, and the names of idols will be destroyed since they have no power.
comments.comment:
This same word could also be applied to the protectors of heresies, who have happened to be full of demons and deceiving spirits. For regarding them the Lawgiver Paul writes thus: 'Some will depart from the healthy faith, paying attention to deceiving spirits and demonic teachings, in the hypocrisy of false prophets, having been cauterized in their own conscience' (1 Timothy 4:1-2).

It is not to be disturbed if the unclean spirit is spoken of in the singular in the prophet, but the deceiving spirits are spoken of in the plural in the Apostolic Scripture. For those things which are taken individually according to each are generally called one spirit. And it is also good to say that the naming of the names of idols is being destroyed, as if their mention were no longer to be, because of their vanity and foolishness, even though they exist only as a designation and not as a power.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Once false prophets are gone, a man who still prophesies in frenzy will be so mocked that even his parents will vote for his death as a false prophet.
comments.comment:
'And it shall come to pass, if a man prophesies any more, his father and his mother who begot him will say to him, "You shall not live, because you have spoken falsely in the name of the Lord"'; and his father and his mother who begot him will run against him in his prophesying (Zechariah 13:3).

Once the false prophets and the unclean spirit have been removed from the earth, if a man should still dare to prophesy out of frenzy and madness, he would be so much a laughingstock and subject to rebuke, that even his parents would not believe him, but would vote for his death, announcing: 'He shall not live anymore because he has spoken falsely upon the name of the Lord,' he being found not a prophet but a false prophet.

By these things, the false prophet is rebuked by his father and his mother, who run against him and join in his downfall, rebuking his sophistries and his deceptive words.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the verse says about parents confronting a false prophet, in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The phrase 'those who begot him in his prophesying' can mean his human parents, or those who brought him up as a false prophet by teaching and imitation, and either way they stand against him.
comments.comment:
Because the phrase 'those who begot him in his prophesying' is ambiguous, it should be expanded into both meanings. One way it might be understood: those who begot him as a man have a disposition toward him as humans guarding parents, because he speaks falsely in the name of the Lord, and they join in his downfall by voting against him. The other way it might be attributed thus: his father and his mother...

They join in mockery against him, those who brought him forth into prophesying, having fathered him as a false prophet through upbringing and procreation, having generated him through imitation and teaching, and who are clearly possessed of a false-prophetic disposition.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The false prophet is called a 'man' because he walks falsely in strife and jealousy according to the flesh.
comments.comment: It is not in vain that such an 'man' has been reproved; rather, because he walks falsely 'in strife and jealousy' according to the flesh, he holds the name of man, similar to those to whom it was said, 'You indeed die as men' (Psalm 82:7), and concerning those unworthy of the Divine Spirit, the Lord says, 'My Spirit shall not remain in these men because they are flesh' (Genesis 6:3).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: False prophets are ashamed when their foretelling fails and their own parents expose them, so that the man, clothed in haircloth, confesses he is no prophet.
comments.comment:
And on that day the prophets shall be ashamed, each from his vision in his prophesying, and they shall put on haircloth instead of those garments by which they lied. And he shall say, 'I am not a prophet, because a man has fathered me from my youth.' And I will say to him, 'Why are these wounds between your hands?' And he shall say, 'Those which were struck in my beloved house.'

Those who promise foreknowledge experience shame because their pre-proclamation is falling away. Since, therefore, the indictment of the false prophet comes not from others alone but also from those who fathered him, for this reason he is ashamed, his prophecy having been exposed, so that he is left to revile himself and to be clothed in haircloth. For a man confesses that he has existed from youth, the youth of which now denotes not age but a young and impetuous character.
comments.selected_reason: Explains the shame of the false prophet in the verses in plain terms.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The 'youth' of the verse is folly, which he asks God to forget, and the man exposed in his false prophecy confesses that he is no prophet.
comments.comment:
For the wicked one, not possessing prudent wisdom nor honorable old age, nor a life without blemish, passes through life with ignorance, according to the proverbial saying: 'Folly is widespread in the heart of a youth, and a rod and instruction are far from him' (Proverbs 22:15). He, finding this state to be the worst, offers a plea to God: 'Do not remember the sinfulness of my youth and my ignorance' (Ps 25:7).

He who is exposed as speaking falsely in prophesying, being ashamed of his vain vision—which is more like divination than true prophecy—confesses that he is not a prophet nor was he advanced from among the prophets to this.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Christ showed his wounds to Thomas so that no unbelief might remain, and in the same way he answers the angels who ask what the wounds in his hands are, that he was struck in the house of his beloved.
comments.comment: He shows himself having wounds and allows him to handle him; for by condescension he so appeared to Thomas though freed of every thickness of body and become light, so that he might be persuaded that it was the same crucified body. And from using Thomas’s words he shows that even when Thomas was saying these things he was present. And even if bodies are raised incorruptible and lacking nothing in the new resurrection, yet so that no word of unbelief may remain, as Thomas sought to see, so he showed; and not only Thomas but also the angels ignorant of the economy [God's plan of salvation] of the incarnation and saying: “Who is this who comes from Edom” and again: “What are these wounds in the midst of your hands?” teaching he says: “with which I was struck in the house of my beloved” (Zechariah 13:6).
comments.selected_reason: Applies the wounds of the verse to Christ's wounds, in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Ammonius of Alexandria

comments.capsule: The Father is said to strike the shepherd because, when the Jews rejected him, he allowed the Son who chose to suffer to suffer, though able to prevent it.
comments.comment: The disciples were troubled not as light people, but because the matter was full of much perplexity and the knowledge of this mystery was hard to grasp — how the one who raised the dead and did countless signs beyond human measure was handed over to so dishonorable a death. This was the one who had said through the prophet, “I will strike the shepherd.” (Zechariah 13:7) (Matthew 26:31) That is why David also says to the Father, “For the one whom you struck, they themselves pursued.” (Psalm 69:26) Yet this did not happen entirely and wholly by the Father’s will; he wanted him not to suffer, if the Jews had accepted him. But since they did not receive him, the Father consented to the Son who chose to suffer this. That is why it is also said that the Father struck “the shepherd,” since he allowed him to suffer though able to prevent his suffering. …
comments.selected_reason: Explains in what sense the Father strikes the shepherd.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria

comments.capsule: Of the captive people two parts are destroyed and the third is tested like silver and gold, and God, hearing it, becomes its God as he was to the patriarchs.
comments.comment:
And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, that two parts shall be destroyed and cut off, but the third shall be left in it; and I will pass through the third through fire and will consume them, as silver is consumed by fire, and I will test them, as gold is tested; he will call upon my name, and I will listen to him, and I will say: This is my people, and he will say: The Lord is my God (Zechariah 13:8-9).

The time is marked by the name of the day, revealing in which the two parts of the captured people shall be destroyed and cut off, the third being shown as tested, passing through fire, and being burned according to how silver is purified and being tested according to how gold is tested. This third of the captives, thus purified and tested, calling upon the name of God, shall have God listening to him and saving him; to whom it will harmoniously belong to reward the people who have been benefited by his listening, God being shown to them in the manner of being their God, as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were. For to all other men God is as Creator, but uniquely to the patriarchs, who worship and revere him.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the two parts and the third refined by fire mean, as the verse words it.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Among the captives some turned to idols, some acted lawlessly as Jews, and a God-fearing remnant was purified by the Divine Word through the purifying fire.
comments.comment:
It is sufficient to consider the division into three of the captured Hebrew people. Many of those deported from their own land and fatherland into the captivity of those who prevailed, having completely turned away from godliness to worship idols, worshipped as if to serve the... and To worship the beast and the dragon, and alongside these, to bow to the mute image of Nebuchadnezzar the tyrant; while others were not doing this, but were acting lawlessly against Judaism and as if they should not change, such as were the elders who remained, adulterously unfaithful, and those who agreed with them against the more prudent Shushan.

Among those who had worshipped idols and were acting lawlessly as Jews, there was another excellent and God-fearing rank in the captivity; they did not fall into dread, nor did they break the law, but were holy and pleasing to God, from whom many men were recorded as saints, of whom are the clearly revealed prophet Zechariah, and Daniel, and those around Azariah, the prophet Ezekiel, and the high priest Jesus [Joshua] the son of Joshedek, and others more, changing through moral virtue and the knowledge of the truth and of God.

The impious parts, two, the Greek and the Jewish, because of what they had done, being a tormentor, are being destroyed and failing, so that through a more strenuous discipline they might cast away the harms that had come upon them. Of this having been done, by the judgment of the divine providence, the third part, being divided from the two parts, is sanctified and made better by the Giver of good things, the Divine Word, being led through the purifying fire and 'burning with the spirit,' concerning which the same One saving all things says: 'I came to cast fire upon the earth, and would I were it were already kindled' (Luke 12:49), and again: 'Every one shall be salted with fire' (Mark 9:49).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Each virtue lies between two faults, excess and deficiency, so those who sin on either side are cut away and the third part is perfected by testing.
comments.comment:
Understand precisely even if a third theory may be said regarding the things set forth. Each of the virtues lies in the middle of two evils, excess and deficiency: courage and temperance, the one being the middle of rashness and cowardice, the other of intemperance and foolishness, just as piety has excess in superstition and deficiency in impiety. Similarly, the free man, being social and giving, has the best middle, of which profligacy is excess and stinginess is deficiency.

And since of those sinning, some by excesses—doing rashness, superstition, and profligacy—and others by deficiencies—doing impiety, cowardice, and stinginess—these two ranks and parts must necessarily be destroyed and cut away having fallen under punishment, the third being perfected, being refined and tested like silver and gold, which is the word and the mind, in order to be tested and perfected according to the following virtues, having surpassed the deficiencies and excesses.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Passing through fire and water without harm is the voice of God at work, so those who are tested like gold and silver have God listening when they call on his name.
comments.comment:
They say they desired salvation: 'O God, you tested us, you burned us like silver is burned; you brought us into a snare, you set tribulations before us'—or 'into our midst'; for it is also carried in many manuscripts—'you brought up men upon our necks, we passed through fire and water, and you brought us out into refreshment.'

Similarly in Isaiah, regarding the one who helps and does good, it says: 'Do not fear, for I am with you; and if you pass through water, rivers shall not overwhelm you; and if you walk through fire, flame shall not burn you, for I am with you' (Isa 43:2). When, then, does anyone pass through fire and remain unharmed, unless he has possessed the voice of God, concerning which it was said: 'The voice of the Lord breaking a flaming fire' (Ps 29:7)? Just as the people crossed the Red Sea with the holy rod without any loss, as the flame of the fire was broken and divided, so the crossing proceeds without being consumed by the flame.

What remained of the third in the Hebrew plurality, the two parts having been destroyed and having ceased, was tested according to the intellect, both gold and silver, passing through fire. Similarly it is carried in Wisdom: 'Just as gold and silver are tested in a furnace, so are chosen hearts before God' (Wis 2:5). The same thought is held by what the apostle Peter writes in his epistle, exhorting to bear tribulations bravely and magnanimously, especially those concerning faith.

And his word has it thus: 'In which rejoice, though you may sometimes be grieved in various trials, so that the testing of your faith may be found more precious than gold being tested by fire; for it shall be found unto praise and glory' (1 Pet 1:6-7). In agreement, James also addresses the disciples of the Gospel: 'Count it all joy, beloved brothers, when you fall into various trials, knowing that the testing of you works patience; and let patience have a perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing' (James 1:4). For thus, having been prepared, those to whom the word is addressed, having been burned like silver according to the word and having been tested like gold according to their own intellect, shall have God listening, calling upon His name, as He benefits them as a people.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what refining like silver and gold means, with Scripture parallels a reader can follow.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: In the Church those who practice superstition and those who Judaize are cut away, so that only the perfect remain as the people of God.
comments.comment:
In the Church of Christ, there are some practicing superstition and others Judaizing among them, even as they also sincerely fear God, in whom the apostles, being said to speak wisdom, have all progressed as far as to reach 'a perfect man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of the knowledge of the Son of God' (Eph 4:13).

The two destroying parts will be cut away, so that they may no longer practice superstition or Judaize according to the ways of the Ebionites. For when this has been endured, only the perfect of the Church will remain in it, so that they indeed may be made 'the people of God' (1 Pet 2:10), and He himself may be confessed as 'their God' (Zechariah 13:9).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: God is incorporeal and unchanging, so when the prophet says the Lord will go forth we do not imagine a changing motion but take such words in harmony with that thought of him.
comments.comment:
God, being incorporeal, rather exceeding all spiritual substance, is without reception of those things pertaining to bodies—colors, forms, and magnitudes—I say, whence he is invisible. For every visible substance must exist under forms, magnitudes, colors, and their adjacents, but God is invisible, as many words of the Scriptures testify, being a spiritual substance, nor does he move transitionally, nor does the whole exist in a place. … Since, therefore, these things are rightly said and thought concerning God, the more bodily things concerning him announced economically in the divine Scriptures must be understood spiritually and appropriately. … 'Every good gift and every perfect gift comes down from above from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change or shadow of turning' (James 1:17). And just as we grasp and understand the words concerning his repentance and his wrath and those of the neighbors, so, since he is incorporeal, we receive the words concerning ascending and descending, and going out and coming in, in harmony with the thought concerning him.

Therefore, in the present prophecy where it is written: 'The Lord will go forth' (Zechariah 14:3), we do not imagine a changing motion; for such motions belong to bodies.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why the verse speaks of the Lord going forth as if he moved, in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The words of God going out, warring and standing with his feet describe his coming among those he manages, as when he goes out to save, and not a bodily motion.
comments.comment: Since, therefore, it does not fit to confess these things concerning an invisible essence, yet they are carried in the divinely inspired oracles, it is necessary to oversee how they must be understood piously. … Being a fountain of goodness and 'full of grace and truth' (John 1:14), the cause of all things, descending in sympathy with those being managed by him, becomes outside himself as if he were among them. For the Lord and our Savior says in the Gospels concerning himself: 'I went out from God and I have come; for I did not come from myself, but he sent me' (John 8:42). With the same thought the prophet Habakkuk spoke toward him: 'You went out for the salvation of your people, to save your anointed ones' (Habakkuk 3:13). … And just as he goes out and comes to those being saved, so much more when he is wroth or wars. For it is written concerning Michael: 'Behold, the Lord goes forth from his house, and he shall be among us for a witness and shall descend' (Micah 1:3), and in Isaiah: 'The Lord of powers will go forth and will crush war, and he will arouse zeal and will cry out against his enemies with strength' (Isaiah 42:13). … Considering these things in a God-befitting manner, God is said to go out 'upon the nations, that he may array himself against them as in a day of war' (Zechariah 14:3) when 'his feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives toward the east' (Zechariah 14:4); for where must his feet stand, since he is no longer moving in indignation, according to what was already previously said: 'And the Lord will sound the trumpet and will go forth in the threat of his wrath' (Zechariah 9:14)? In this way, Adam heard the voice of the feet of God, the fearful one, having received the sensation of him leaving and walking away from him who previously was with him and conversing with him. …
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The branches that fell through unfaithfulness are torn apart, as is said of the ruined Jewish city, while believers are to become a fruitful olive in God's house and imitators of Christ, whose name is 'rising'.
comments.comment:
Regarding the unfaithful branches having come to the sea and being torn apart by a very strong wind, it is said concerning this ruined city—the Jewish one, I say—and by another prophet, who is Micah, by God: "I will scatter the stones of it into chaos and I will uncover its foundations" (Micah).

When these gloomy things have come upon the wretched synagogue of the Jews, it is necessary for us, those having believed in the Savior, to become a fruitful olive in the house of God and toward the rising in the mount of olives, so that we may also be transferred into the divine paradise by the grace of God, becoming imitators of Christ, concerning whom it is written: "Behold, a man, rising is his name" (Zechariah 6:12).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The north in the verse is the evil power, rather Satan himself, and the south is the Savior, to whom the bride calls when the cold north hinders the flow of the divine aromas.
comments.comment:
"Half of the mountain shall lean toward the north and half of it toward the south. And the gorge of my mountains shall be blocked, and the gorge of my mountains shall be joined up as far as Asher, just as it was blocked in the days of the earthquake in the days of King Uzziah of Judah" (Zechariah 14:5).

The half, he says, of the mountain—clearly the mount of olives—will lean toward the north, toward the one deviating into the sea and the chaos, the other half reaching toward the south.

What are the north and the south? From the Breath of Breaths [the Song of Songs], the Church having been ravished by her own bridegroom, is to learn, saying: "Arise, north, and come, south, blow upon my garden and let my aromas flow."

The north in these things is the evil power, rather Satan himself; the south, being the Savior himself, is approached as the bridegroom. Therefore, when the very cold north is present, the flow of the divine aromas is hindered, the pores being choked because they become thickened due to the coldness of the north and become hard; the bride flees from this and calls to the south, so that by his warmth …
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the north and the south of the divided mountain stand for in the writer's reading.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The north wind is called to rise in the faithful soul by turning away from evil, and the south wind is entreated to come so that the soul draws near to God, who then draws near to it.
comments.comment:
From the sources of the intelligible, the fragrances flow, concerning which it is said toward the bridal chamber of the spiritual spouse: 'The fragrance of your myrrh is above all spices' (Song of Solomon 1:3). The north wind is said to have heat and to be an invigorating breath, having learned that fire exists and came to cast upon the earth, as he himself announced saying: 'I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled' (Luke 12:49).

It must be said: 'Arise, north wind,' not by voice alone but in reality, so that it may be sent from afar. In deeds, he says: 'Arise, north wind,' to the faithful soul saying to the teacher who speaks: 'Turn away from evil and do good,' and to the Apostle who wrote to the whole Church: 'Test all things, hold fast to the good. Abstain from every kind of evil' (1 Thessalonians 5:21-22). The north wind, driving the abstention from every kind of evil and the turning away from evil, urges the south wind to come so as to draw near to it through pious faith and moral virtue. For thus, to those being thus prepared, the provider of all good things comes, as the theologian James wrote: 'Draw near to God and He will draw near to you' (James 4:8).

Having the longing for His presence, and being near to: 'Come, south wind,' in that bridal drama he hints: 'Come, my sister, let us go out to the field' (Song of Solomon 7:11). This is equivalent to: 'Arise, north wind, and come, south wind,' and to: 'Draw near to God and He will draw near to you, resist the devil and he will flee from you' (James 4:7-8), as the one resisting the devil says to him: 'Arise, north wind,' and the one drawing near to God entreating the south wind to come to him, the God Logos, concerning whom in the song of the prophet Habakkuk, according to some interpreters, it is brought forth instead of: 'God will come from Thaman,' as 'God will come from the south wind,' the coming of the Father from the south wind of the bride, according to that which is said by Him in the Gospel: 'He who receives me receives him who sent me' (John 13:20). For in whatever way he who sees Him sees the Father, so the one receiving Him receives the Father abiding in Him, in whom is His Only-begotten.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The mountains of God are heights of knowledge and of practical life, and the gorge, the depth of things spoken in riddles, was smoothed by Christ's teaching so that the mountains are joined.
comments.comment:
Regarding his mountains, the prophets have said in accordance with the subject that there is a height belonging to them not only of knowledge and wisdom, but also of the application of practical life. For concerning these things, the hymn-singer spoke of the origin of all: 'You shine wondrously from eternal mountains' (Psalm 76:4). How could they not be eternal mountains, from which God wondrously illuminates the knowledge of the truth and broadly the knowledge concerning the Trinity, those who gaze upon unseeing eternal things according to the apostolic exhortation (2 Cor 4:18)?

The abyss of the depth of the obscurity of those things spoken in enigma is a gorge of these mountains, which he who came to fulfill the law and the prophets (Matt 5:17) has unblocked, having leveled with his own teaching and presence the rough and uneven ground of those things spoken with concealment, so that it might appear easy to traverse through smoothness. This having happened, the gorge of the mountains was joined to the text through the appearing of harmony, up to Asaph, who was called 'deaf to the feet' because of the speed of his walking, according to the sharp-seeing gaze; for this animal is perceptive, as the appellation itself shows from the word 'gazing'. Therefore, up to Asaph, the connection of the mountains will be known to the discerning.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: No earthquake is recorded in Uzziah's reign, so the verse is read of the shaking when he tried to burn incense himself in the temple and was struck.
comments.comment: In the same way, the obstruction of the mountains has occurred as in the days of the earthquake, which existed in the days of Uzziah, the king of Judah. We have not found a perceptible earthquake having occurred at all while Uzziah was reigning, neither in the Kingdoms nor in the Chronicles; therefore, what is written about him must be understood allegorically. And see lest a shaking occurred during Uzziah, intending to seize the priesthood for himself. For having entered into the temple of God, and having approached the holy altar, he attempts to offer sacrifice through himself and not through the priests (2 Chron 26:16). The daily priest, most boldly asserting this transgression, while coinciding with the others, saying: 'It is not yours, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but that of the priests,' he was distressed, and he stretched out his hand with anger to be seized by the guards to harm them; but immediately his hand was struck, as if to cast the tyrant out of the temple instantly, having been struck by the holy place as far as the porch, because of his insolence.
comments.selected_reason: Explains the earthquake in Uzziah's days which the verse mentions.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The earthquake is tied by Jewish tradition to Isaiah's vision in the year King Uzziah died, a shaking toward the better that ended the king's seizing of the priestly service.
comments.comment: The earthquake now being declared lies also at the beginning of the prophet Amos: 'For words,' says Amos, 'which came from Tekoa, two years before the earthquake in the days of Ozias,' the earthquake being said here, according to the circulating Jewish tradition, of the vision appearing to Isaiah, concerning which it has been written thus: 'It happened in the year in which King Ozias died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a high and lifted-up throne, and Seraphim were standing around him, six wings to the one and six wings to the other' (Isa 6:1-2), and after a little: 'And the other cried to the other: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Sabaoth, full is the heaven and the earth of his glory' (Isa 6:3). … For how could there not be a shaking of change toward the better having happened by the seeing of God, so that the heaven and the earth might be filled with his glory, and a removal might occur of the lawlessness of the one discovered in seeing the divine vision, and a remission of the sins of all the people? … In the days of the death of Ozias, who desired to plunge the divine laws, desiring to seize for himself the priestly service not fitting to him, there was attached that which he had newly cut through by a cleavage of the laws, so that the priest might again unhinderedly perform his own things in the temple, and the king, attending to the protection of those in authority, was no longer touching the priestly things because the care of the holy things was not to be held by him.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The day with no light, neither day nor night, is the day of the cross, when darkness fell at midday and light returned toward evening, and the living water flows from Christ's side to baptism and repentance.
comments.comment:
“You shall fear day and night”: for day and night were the same, because “there was darkness over all the land from the sixth hour” (Matthew 27:45). Hence Zechariah is at a loss what he ought rather to name it, what it is fitting to call it: whether the time of the cross should take its name from the darkness that fell or from the daylight that by rule belonged to it. So he says: “And on that day there shall be no light; and there shall be cold and frost. It is a great day; it shall be known to the Lord; not day nor night; and toward evening there shall be light. And on that day living water shall go out from Jerusalem, half of it to the first sea and half of it to the last sea” (Zechariah 14:6-8). These things happened both visibly and spiritually.

“On that day there shall be no light”: for the sun set at midday, and darkness and ignorance had been poured over the hearts of the Jews. “There shall be cold and frost.” Peter bears witness to this, warming himself by the charcoal fire because the winter season was at its height (John 18:18). But beyond this there was cold and frost, because the love of the Jews toward God had then grown especially cold; for otherwise they would not have crucified the Savior and Redeemer who came from him. “It is a great day.” How could it not be great, the day on which Adam was formed anew, sin was abolished, death was destroyed, the potter received back his vessel, the shepherd his sheep, the merchant his pearl? “It shall be known to God.” For how could he who knows all things not recognize above all that day, on which he gave up his only-begotten Son for sacrifice? “Not day nor night”: since by its course it was day, not night. “Toward evening there shall be light”: when, after the ninth hour, the darkness ceased. So the same time was both night and day.

“And living water shall go out from Jerusalem.” From where? From the side of the Life (John 19:34); for from the place where Eve was formed, from there the Church is fittingly formed (Genesis 2:21-22). “Half of it into the first sea”: that is, the sea of baptism. “And half of it into the last sea”: plainly, the sea of repentance.
comments.selected_reason: Explains the verse as describing the darkness at the cross, in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Hesychius of Jerusalem

comments.capsule: In the spring of the gospel we celebrate Passover and Pentecost, and the living water Christ gives becomes a spring in the one who drinks, from whom rivers flow.
comments.comment:
Because a spiritual spring has arrived, and the remainder of the month of new moons has come, we celebrate the feast of passing, called Passover by the Hebrew voice, in which Christ is hidden, so that, bearing his spiritual flesh and his holy blood, we might 'celebrate the feast with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth' (1 Cor 5:8), through which we shall also complete the festival of the high feast and that of the weeks, called Pentecost, in which we shall reap perfect gleanings and most full ears from those that blossomed in the spring.

Concerning both of the seasons, the holy one said, praising God: 'You prepared sun and moon, harvest and spring, you made these, remember your creation' (Ps 74:17) … A testimony of water becoming living is taken from the Gospel of the Savior, who said: 'But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him shall become in him a spring of water living, leaping into eternal life' (John 4:14), and again: 'He who believes in me, just as the scripture said, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly' (John 7:38). For just as the one drinking from the water which Jesus gives shall have a spring of living water in him, so rivers of living water shall flow from the belly of the one drinking.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: When the Only-begotten comes and all error is abolished, the one true God will be confessed, as Paul says God is of the Gentiles as well as the Jews since God is one.
comments.comment:
In that day the Lord shall be one, and His name one. … When the aforementioned things exist as a gift of God, the polytheism of such a kind will be destroyed, by the one alone having composed all things and being known and confessed. For in the past, while there was difference between the last and first sea, the calling of the Jews and the Greeks—for these seas were given—it was not confessed by all that there is one God. … But when the gospel has come, the knowledge of the one and only progenitor has risen above men, as Paul, speaking in Christ, writes: 'Is God not only of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles? Yes, also of the Gentiles, since God is one' (Romans 3:29-30). For this is what it signifies, that God is one.

Therefore, on the day in which the expected one, the Only-begotten Son of God, is to come, with all error and false glory being abolished, the one and only true God shall be confessed, so that those having possessed the knowledge of the truth may alone worship and serve him, since the works of hands are no longer being called gods, as the divine Logos says: 'The gods who did not make the heaven and the earth, let them perish from the earth and from under the heaven' (Jeremiah 10:11).
comments.selected_reason: Explains what 'the Lord shall be one and his name one' means, in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: God's oneness will be known not only when false gods are refuted but when no one still worships the world or any part of it instead of the Creator, and then his one name is praised in all the earth.
comments.comment:
Not only, therefore, when these pseudonymous gods have been refuted by no longer being supposed to be gods will the one God be known, 'having turned' the apostates 'from idols to serve the living and true God' (1 Thessalonians 1:9), but also by being piously seen that neither the world is God, nor any part of it, nor are men still worshipping or revering the creation instead of the Creator, so as no longer to worship the sun and the moon or serve them.

In this way, the oneness of God will remain, on the day in which the sun of righteousness makes and shows himself, and his name will be one. For it is signified by one name, being in agreement with the exact thought and having piety of all, the fulfillment of what was said in the hymns: 'Wonderful is your name in all the earth' (Ps 8:1), and again: 'You have magnified your holy name above all' (Psalm 138:2), and again: 'As your name, O God, so is your praise to the ends of the earth' (Psalm 48:10). In agreement with the hymn, the prophet Habakkuk also says these things concerning the true God: 'The earth is full of his praise' (Habakkuk 3:3).
