comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Anathema can mean a prohibition or a thing set apart to God, and when Jerusalem dwells securely no one will be anathematized in it and the carved and earthen things will be destroyed.
comments.comment:
When the prohibition is shown by the wording, and when the thing set apart and confessed to God is shown. Regarding the former, it should be said as it is written: 'If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be anathema' (1 Cor 16:22), and as it is: 'No one speaking by the Spirit of God says: Anathema Jesus' (1 Cor 12:3). For this being the meaning, Paul wished 'to be anathema for the brothers and kinsmen according to the flesh' (Rom 9:3). And regarding the latter being signified: of the word anathema, there are many things to gather from the history of the Scriptures, which the philologist can discover for himself.

When Jerusalem dwells with certainty, no one will be anathematized in it, and no foundation will remain, for the carved things and the earthen things will have been destroyed. For these things having become outside, it shall dwell certainly having the spiritual safety, concerning which the prophet Jeremiah expressed, having said: 'And blessed shall be the man who has trusted in the Lord' (Jer 17:7).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Those who besiege Jerusalem will fail in their flesh while standing, from hunger, thirst and the evils they expect, until their eyes come out of their sockets and their tongue fails.
comments.comment: And this shall be the fall, which the Lord will cut off all the peoples who turned against Jerusalem; their flesh shall fail while they are standing on their feet, and their eyes shall run out from their sockets, and their tongue shall fail in their mouths (Zech 14:12). This fall is for those who have encamped against it and surround it with trenches. What indeed is it that he foretells for those circling the beautiful city Jerusalem? They shall fail, he says, their flesh standing on their feet, that is, from much hunger or thirst of the expected evils and calamities. To this extent indeed the failure of their flesh shall be, as to hide their eyes and for them to come out of the sockets and for their tongue to fail in their mouth.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the plague on Jerusalem's besiegers in the verse means.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The same fate came on those who persecuted the Church, and God strikes besiegers so that they fall from their superstitious worship and, as Simeon said of Christ, rise to stand firm in faith.
comments.comment:
But this wickedness has exceeded not only those who circled and besieged the sensible Jerusalem, but also those who persecuted the Christian … and the Church of Christ, Jerusalem being viewed by way of an ascent. The history of Christians contains many things both terrible and true; they were judged by divine decree against those who attacked the servants of God and the gathering places, to scatter them into the ground and deliver the divine books to fire. More extensively regarding such things has been treated for us in the commentaries on Isaiah, which we send forward to the beautiful ones for reading as an exhortation.

God strikes those who surrounded Jerusalem by way of wars, so that they might fall from the steady state which they guarded by remaining in superstitious worship. When this fall occurs profitably, a resurrection and a standing shall be received, having praises exceeding all.

Concerning this vision, having been filled with the Holy Spirit, the justified Simeon, receiving into his arms the infant born of the virgin Mary, says that he shows this: 'Behold, this lies for a fall and a resurrection of many' (Luke 2:34-35).

For on his account they fall, and the fleshly ones, so that having been raised according to the holiness of God they might be shown secure, having been firmly established in faith and other virtue, according to that which was written by the Apostle to the ecclesiastical ones: 'In faith you have stood' (1 Cor 16:13). And this standing occurs with the Savior Jesus; for it is to him that one must learn, saying: 'There are some of those standing here who shall by no means taste death' (Matthew 16:28).

Those thus benefited cast off the fleshly mindset and the eyes seeing badly, so that they might no longer be in the flesh, but in the spirit, and no longer live wickedly and adulterously, but uprightly and soberly, killing the deeds of the body with the spirit and turning the eyes away from vanity, lifting them toward God so as to say: 'To you I lifted up my eyes, you who dwell in heaven' (Ps 123:1) …
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Those who see sinfully have their eyes dimmed so that those who see rightly may see, the Jews being blinded for denying the Lord while those called from the Gentiles are enlightened, and the tongue is ordered to speak righteousness.
comments.comment:
Similarly, according to the theory applied, one should attempt to take what was said in the Gospel by our Savior, as previously brought forward: 'I came into the world for judgment, so that those not seeing might see and those seeing might become blind' (John 9:39). For the eyes of those seeing sinfully, having hardened their vision, there will be a dimming regarding seeing rightly and holily.

It is possible also to apply another understanding to the Gospel. Since the Jews, blaspheming the Lord impiously while unfaithfully denying Him, it was fitting that they be blinded, according to what was said in a prophet: 'The servants of God were blinded' (Isaiah 42:19), those falsely promising to serve Him; and when this happened, those called from the Gentiles into faith rose up, since it had come to pass that he said: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me, having sent me to preach to the poor, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind' (Luke 4:18), having enlightened them with His own wisdom, according to what is written: 'The wisdom of a man lights up his face' (Ecclesiastes 8:1).

One should also take up what was proclaimed in the Psalms: 'The Lord makes the wise blind' (Ps 146:8), so that they might no longer be shown as blind but as seeing sharply, once the eyes of those seeing wickedly have been hindered and have fallen away from their own pupils—and these are the natural meanings—the eyes that see God. Man raises these eyes toward Him just as he says: 'To You I lifted up my eyes, You who dwell in heaven' (Ps 123:1).

After the flesh has been subdued, whose mindset is enmity toward God, and of those seeing impiously with eyes flowing from the interpreted pupils, so that those seeing sharply may be shown, concerning whom the Apostle writes the word having this expression: 'The eyes of the heart having been enlightened' (Eph 1:18), it is said in harmony that the tongue should also be ordered in the mouth of those having a harmful and material-matter-centered speech, so that what is said by the wise to the Master of all may exist: 'My tongue shall meditate on Your righteousness alone' (Psalm 71:24).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The 'great ecstasy of the Lord' means a wonder, as in Hosea and Habakkuk, coming from the Lord upon those who are benefited.
comments.comment: In the day of the Lord, what the prophet taught was accomplished: a great ecstasy of the Lord upon them, the Lord granting it, the ecstasy here declaring a wonder through negligence and thoughtlessness. For in the prophet Hosea, what is written: 'The sons of Israel shall turn and shall seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they shall stand astonished at the Lord and at His good things' (Hosea 3:5), declares a wonder, or, as some have said, a marvel. Of the same thought exists also that which is written by Habakkuk: 'I have understood your works and was astonished' (Habakkuk 3:2). The prophet says that the ecstasy thus interpreted having come from the Lord upon those being benefited, has become enlarged.
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the 'ecstasy' of the verse means, in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Judah arrayed in Jerusalem is the confessing believer who gathers the gold, silver and garments of all the peoples, meaning the enlightened mind, the exact word, the virtues, doctrines and mysteries of piety.
comments.comment:
And Judah will array himself in Jerusalem and will gather the strength of all the peoples around him, gold and silver and clothing in a very great multitude. … When this happens, 'Judah will array himself in Jerusalem,' concerning which it was said: 'Judah, your brothers praised you,' the Judah who confesses above all. But the receiving Judah arrays himself, confessing in the true Jerusalem, in which 'he who dwells shall not be shaken for ever,' in order to gather around him the strength of all the peoples, gold and silver and a multitude of garments, which is very great.

Often it has been made clear also in other divinely inspired writings, and to the prophet who is set forth for examination, to signify the mind enlightened by the sign of gold and the prudent and exact word by the analogy of silver. Therefore it is appropriate to apply fittingly the gold and the silver and the garments, the great multitude of which the holy Judah has gathered around him from all the peoples, that is, from all those having believed from the nations.

For clothing and garments, according to divine analogy, are the virtues according to kind and the actions performed according to them, and the doctrines of piety and the mysteries of the truth. With these garments she is covered: the bride of Christ, being the Church, and a queen, as it is sung in the forty-fourth and fourth Psalm: 'The queen stood at your right hand, arrayed and adorned in gold' (Psalm 45:9) …
comments.selected_reason: Explains what the gold, silver and garments gathered by Judah stand for.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The garments the Spirit teaches clothe the inner man, as in Ecclesiastes and Isaiah, and Judah gathers the spiritual treasures of the peoples in great abundance.
comments.comment:
For the Holy Spirit does not teach regarding bodily pleasures to such an extent as to think so, but rather regarding garments that clothe and adorn the inner man, about which it is commanded in Ecclesiastes: 'Let your garments always be white' (Eccl 9:8), which God himself clothes and endows the soul that speaks thankfully: 'I will rejoice in the Lord; for he has clothed me with the garment of salvation and the robe of gladness' (Isaiah 61:10).

Toward this one swelling with worldly pleasures, the one providing her the same as a bridegroom says: 'I have clothed you in fine linen and purple' (Ezekiel 16:10), fine linen being the beautiful and subtle thoughts and works woven out, and purple being the actions and words of the senses woven together, like the purple growing from the earth, so as to be compared to the sensible things.

Judah, being arrayed as a gathering, seeing the peace of the strong Jerusalem by intellect, gathered the spiritual treasures of the people which are gold, silver, and a great abundance of garments, clearly signifying the mind and the word according to the interpretations by allegory, and the provided clothing being gathered in great abundance.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The horses and other animals fall from their present state in order to rise to good, the mares that lusted after their neighbors' mates falling from adultery to rise in a praiseworthy resurrection.
comments.comment:
And this shall be the fall of the horses and the mules and the camels and the donkeys and all the cattle that are in those encampments, according to this fall (Zech 14:15).

Just as nations that stood badly have fallen blessedly and risen praiseworthily, as it was correctly interpreted, so the horses, mules, camels, and donkeys according to allegory, having fallen from their current state, will rise salvationally upon a special good.

For the mares having become those that lust after the mates of their neighbors, they have fallen from the passion of the lover and the state of adultery, in order that they might rise in a praiseworthy resurrection, concerning which Jesus said to those being instructed: 'Arise, let us go from here' (John 14:31), and toward the Church having become his bride from the nations he cries: 'Arise, come, my beloved' (Song 2:10). The apostolic teaching possesses this understanding here: 'Arise, you who sleep, and rise from the dead' (Eph 5:14)...
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The mules, camels and donkeys likewise fall and rise: the mule is sterile of soul, and the camels are students of the law who do not distinguish what is to be practiced, as the Jews according to the flesh do not.
comments.comment:
Similarly to the fall of horses, the mules will also fall, because of a sterility of soul, such as they are called. Concerning both of these animals, the divine Word says to men: "Do not become like the horse and the mule, which have no understanding." (Psalm 32:9). Just as the promiscuous and the many-partnered are called horses, so too a mule might be said allegorically of a virgin possessing an incorrupt body, though not necessarily being holy in the Spirit. Because of such a sterility, even the one who has been castrated is called a mule, not for the sake of the kingdom of heaven, but for the sake of pleasing men.

After the fall, the horses and mules, having been assigned that role, will rise up and will have the power to charge against those for whom the saints said: "Mount upon your horses, and your cavalry is salvation." (Habakkuk 3:8). Likewise, the mule will undergo the transformation interpreted by David, whom I call the Savior, riding and charging royally.

In the same manner, the camels and the donkeys and all the other cattle found in those encampments, as is clearly shown, will fall down and rise up. According to the fall of the horses and those called as such, men who study the divine law by rote, but without distinguishing what is to be practiced from what is not, are camels according to tropology.

For indeed, the students of the law, who lift up words by 'nibbling' and devouring 'as if chaff' the pre-laid food, do not break the weapon nor sharpen the claw; they are found to be unclean, not distinguishing the practice from the non-practice. Such are the Jews according to the flesh, who do not divide the Spirit from the letter, nor the truth from the shadow, nor even the things being clearly performed from those being acted out through wickedness, whence it is thus: They are considered a "sinful nation and a people full of sins," because there is not enough for purity from emptiness, that is, to study in vain, according to that which is said concerning them: "The people have studied in vain." (Psalm 2:1). For having been born outside the instruction of the one "who begot them and exalted them," all heard as one: "A son who abandons the keeping of his father's instruction will meditate on evil words." (Proverbs 19:27).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The feast of booths is fulfilled in our bodies as tents, in the pure marriage bed, and most of all in the resurrection, kept as rest joining the seven of the old covenant and the eight of Christ's resurrection.
comments.comment:
Regarding the revealed understanding, the feast of the booths must be understood otherwise. Our human bodies are thus presented. Immediately indeed the most holy Peter, a disciple of Christ, writes: 'The Lord Jesus Christ revealed to me that the removal of my dwelling is near' (2 Peter 1:14). In agreement also the lawgiver Paul says: 'We who are in the tent groan, being weighed down, because we do not wish to be stripped off but to be clothed, so that the mortal might be swallowed up by life' (2 Cor 5:4).

Moreover the feast of the booths is fulfilled previously and especially by those promising 'rejoicing', not by men alone with women not having been defiled, but also by women hastening to have holiness in spirit and body.

In addition to these, those entering the honorable marriage also adorn their own booths, being pure and guarding their bed undefiled.

Furthermore, the festival of the booths is fulfilled even more highly, being crowned and made glorious in the expected time of the resurrection, of the corruptible body being raised incorruptible and of the psychic spiritual body being raised. Does not the body become a divine booth, sown in weakness and dishonor, so that it might rise in power and glory?

It is worthy to learn how this spiritual feast is celebrated on the fifteenth of the seventh month. For the celebrant must, through the interpreted booths, surpass the cosmos made in six days, resting from all service of worship, sabbath-keeping according to the 'Sabbath having been given to the people of God', which Jesus alone confirms saying: 'I will give you all who come rest' (Matt 11:28), and again: 'You will find rest for your souls' (Matt 11:29).

On the fifteenth day of this seventh month, those celebrating are 'those who have given a portion to the seven and also to the eight', adhering to the old and the new covenant; for through the seven the old is signified because of sabbath-keeping, but through the eight is the resurrection of Christ after the cross, having occurred on the eighth day, the Lord's day.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Only those whose citizenship is in heaven ascend to the Jerusalem above, while those who still think of earthly things do not ascend and are added to the nations that did not.
comments.comment:
Since the spiritual Jerusalem lies on high according to the philosophy of the writing Apostle, where it says: 'But the Jerusalem above', and where it says: 'You have ascended to Zion, the mountain and city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem', only those are ascending upon it who are able to say: 'But our citizenship is in the heavens' (Phil 3:20), and again: 'He raised us up' (Eph 2:6), God clearly, 'and seated us in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus' (Eph 2:6), while those of the tribes of the earth who are still 'bearing the image of the swine' (1 Corinthians 15:49) and 'thinking of earthly things' (Philippians 3:19) exist and are not ascending to see the beautiful city lying on high in peace.

Those not ascending shall be added to those from among all the nations who did not ascend, being persuaded by the same things as them.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Those who ascend will worship the King, Lord Pantokrator, with the angels, and the title belongs to the whole Trinity, so we should not stay among the tribes of the earth but store up the heart in heaven.
comments.comment:
Those thinking of earthly things who are not ascending because they are being carried down by the weight of earthly works, those having hurried to ascend into the city having broken foundations, through the one laying the foundation, the 'artisan and builder of it, the Lord' (Hebrews 11:10), shall worship the King Lord the Pantokrator with the angels. For it has been written: 'All the angels of God shall worship him' (Hebrews 1:6).

A Lord existing as a King and Pantokrator is declared not the Father without the Son nor the Son without the Father. For one kingdom and lordship is the same, and the pantokratic power is the same of the Trinity. Therefore, if a desire enters into us to worship the Trinity as King Lord Pantokrator, let us not remain among the tribes of the earth, but having stored up the heart there in heaven, so that we might... being in Jerusalem, we might worship with all the rational creation, 'bowing every knee to the King of the heavens and earth and those under the earth, for the glory of God the Father, every tongue confessing that Jesus is Lord' (Philippians 2:10).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The basins are the spiritual bowls of fragrance, the divine writings or their thoughts, and when they become bowls every basin is holy in Jerusalem, the glorious Church, and in Judah.
comments.comment:
Concerning the spiritual bowls, in the Song of Songs the divine bride says concerning her brother: 'My sister has come down into his garden to shepherd the bowls of fragrance in gardens and to gather lilies' (Song of Solomon 6:2). Some ask whether the bowls of fragrance into which the brother has descended are the divinely inspired writings, or rather their divine thoughts, in which the one who descended shepherds in gardens and gathers lilies bearing a spiritual fragrance of lilies being presented.

When the basins become bowls of fragrance before the face of the spiritual altar, then in this way every basin shall be holy in holy Jerusalem and in Judah. In this, Jerusalem is to be understood as the glorious Church, and Judah as he whom his brothers praise and whom the sons of his father worship. Who this is, is said in those things previously read from the prophet.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: All who offer the sacrifice of righteousness and of praise come to the one they worship to glorify him.
comments.comment: 'And all those who sacrifice shall come and take from them and eat from them. And there shall no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord of the Universe on that day' (Zechariah 14:21). All those performing the sacrifice of righteousness and the sacrifice of praise shall come to the one being worshiped and whom they serve, in order to glorify him, who exhorts them to this. For he says: 'A sacrifice of praise shall glorify me' (Psalm 50:23).
comments.selected_reason: Explains who the sacrificers of the verse are, in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Those who sacrifice come together in harmony to serve as priests, taking from the sanctified basins, and because this service is done with discourse and learned contemplation the basins are called bowls.
comments.comment: And they shall come together in mutual accord, with harmonious purpose, to perform the priestly service together, taking from the sanctified basins set around the altar … so as to boil the victims' meat in them, as already said. And since the service of the basins in question is accomplished with discourse and learned contemplation, they are rightly called bowls. For that this figure signifies discourse is proclaimed in the Song of Songs: the bride, revealing in her soul the beauty and loveliness of the beloved she loved, says, 'His cheeks are like bowls of spice, yielding perfumes' (Song 5:13).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: A Canaanite is the stranger from the womb who stands outside piety and will no longer be in the Lord's house, either by changing into a true Israelite or by being cast out, as the lawless man was put out at Corinth.
comments.comment:
This mystical, intellectual worship being performed by those arriving to perform the spiritual liturgy, having cast the meats taken by analogy—namely those from calves and rams—into the holy vessels, a Canaanite shall no longer be in the house of the Lord Almighty on the day when the restoration of those … has occurred. For a Canaanite is the stranger from the womb as one being outside of piety; and he shall not be, either by changing into Israel, 'the true one not having deceit,' or by being cast out of the house of the Lord Almighty. A Canaanite is to be accepted allegorically even if he has fallen out of the Israelite state. Such was the other, according to Sossannus, a man staying as an elder, to whom the most wise Daniel says: 'Seed of Canaan and not Judah, your beauty has deceived you, and desire has turned your heart; thus you did to the daughters of Israel, and there they fear to consort with you, but a daughter of Judah did not endure your lawlessness' (Susanna 1:56). Hosea also agrees regarding the lawless ones, as if they were Canaanites having such a condition: 'Ephraim has set himself a stumbling block as a companion of idols. He desired Canaanites; by committing fornication, he has become a fornicator' (Hosea 4:17).

And since the lawless one is, according to tropology, a Canaanite, he is cast out of the holy house of the Lord Almighty, so that he may no longer be in it. The divine apostle Paul fulfills this in his letter to the Corinthian Church: 'For it is heard among you that there is fornication, and such fornication, which even is not among the Gentiles, that a man has the wife of his father. And you are such, and should not rather have mourned, so that the one who has done this thing might be removed from among you' (1 Corinthians 5:1, 5).
comments.selected_reason: Explains who the 'Canaanite' of the verse is, in the writer's reading.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind
